_note: Canonical decomposition of Bihzad's Yusuf fleeing Zulaykha (Cairo, Adab Farsi 22, f. 52b) into interactable elements. Boxes are generated from imagelab/data/regions.json - edit there, then re-run games/yusuf-ascent/build_palace.py. Rung assignments are this project's interpretation and are labelled as such in the portal.

source.title: Yūsuf fleeing Zulaykha
source.manuscript: Būstān of Saʿdī, made for Sultan Ḥusayn Bāyqarā
source.institution: Egyptian National Library and Archives, Cairo
source.rights: Public domain (PD-Art): faithful photographic reproduction of a two-dimensional public-domain work, via Wikimedia Commons.

rungs.name: Mulk
rungs.gloss: The kingdom of sense — brick, street, the door onto the road.

rungs.name: Threshold
rungs.gloss: The iwan and its tilework: the sensible world already arranged into pattern.

rungs.name: Barzakh
rungs.gloss: The isthmus. Stairs belong to neither storey they join — the picture's clearest structural pun.

rungs.name: ʿĀlam al-khayāl
rungs.gloss: The imaginal: forms held as images. Doors, cartouches, the lapis court.

rungs.name: Malakūt
rungs.gloss: The angelic realm — the parts of the building carried on nothing.

rungs.name: Jabarūt
rungs.gloss: The chamber where the flight happens; power, not place.

rungs.name: Lāhūt
rungs.gloss: The crown. Finial, cupola, and the flame that is the only light in the picture.

nodes.title: The folio entire
nodes.card: Cairo, Egyptian National Library, Adab Farsi 22, f. 52b. Herat, 893/1488, for Sultan Ḥusayn Bāyqarā. The painting takes the whole written surface and drives its verses into the architecture instead of around it.
nodes.label: The complete folio

nodes.title: The palace, whole
nodes.card: Nothing in this building is structurally possible, and every surface is finished to the same degree of attention. That combination is the argument: it is a diagram wearing the costume of a house.
nodes.label: The impossible palace — the whole structure

nodes.title: The crowning kiosk
nodes.card: An octagonal kiosk with a finial, on a roof no stair in the picture reaches. It is the terminus of the ascent and the one part of the palace no figure can occupy.
nodes.label: Crowning octagonal kiosk with finial — the roof above the roof

nodes.title: The inscribed cornice
nodes.card: A tiled eaves band carrying nastaʿlīq. Epigraphy at the roofline follows the wall plane rather than the page — the text is built into the building, not laid over it.
nodes.label: Blue-tiled eaves band and inscribed cornice

nodes.title: The unreachable turret
nodes.card: A blue-and-white turret at the upper right. No door, stair or landing in the composition connects to it. It is reachable only by looking.
nodes.label: Blue-and-white turreted kiosk, upper right — a tower reachable from nowhere

nodes.title: The upper chamber
nodes.card: The one enclosed room in the picture, and the smallest area of actual narrative. Saʿdī's Būstān describes no palace at all; the chamber comes from Jāmī's Yūsuf u Zulaykhā, finished in 1483, five years before this page.
nodes.label: The upper chamber — the moment of flight

nodes.title: The white arch
nodes.card: The only large unpatterned surface in the folio. Bihzād reserves blankness for the exact place where the event happens.
nodes.label: White pointed arch of the upper chamber

nodes.title: Yūsuf
nodes.card: Mid-stride, one arm flung up, moving left and out of the chamber. In Jāmī the doors give way at the touch of his pointing finger; in Qur'an 12:23 Zulaykha has locked them and they open regardless.
nodes.label: Yusuf in green, flame-haloed, mid-stride

nodes.title: The flame-halo
nodes.card: A gold flame nimbus. It is the only light source in a picture with no modelled light anywhere else: illumination here marks ontological rank, not optics.
nodes.label: Yusuf's flame-halo — the only light source in the picture

nodes.title: Zulaykha
nodes.card: Leaning after him, a hand on his skirt. Jāmī's reading inverts the moral — she is the Sufi lover whose ruinous desire is finally redeemed into union, not simply the temptress of the older telling.
nodes.label: Zulaykha in orange, reaching after him

nodes.title: Chamber revetment
nodes.card: Dark-ground floral tile on the chamber's left wall. In Jāmī the seven chambers are hung with paintings of Yūsuf and Zulaykha themselves — images of the story inside the story.
nodes.label: Blue floral tile revetment, chamber's left wall

nodes.title: The floor under the flight
nodes.card: A patterned panel directly beneath Yūsuf's feet, drawn in a projection that disagrees with the walls enclosing it.
nodes.label: Patterned floor panel under Yusuf's feet

nodes.title: The tasselled sill
nodes.card: The chamber's floor ends in a ledge over open air. Whatever Yūsuf is striding toward, the painting gives him no floor to stride onto.
nodes.label: The chamber sill — tasselled ledge over open air

nodes.title: The red balcony
nodes.card: A cantilevered pavilion at the right, framed in vermilion. It overlaps the chamber's storey but does not share a level with it.
nodes.label: The red cantilevered balcony

nodes.title: The balcony door
nodes.card: An arched opening in the balcony's back wall, giving onto a plane with no depth behind it.
nodes.label: Arched doorway in the balcony's back wall

lock.prompt: This door is painted on a plane with nothing behind it.
lock.gloss: A blind. Not every opening in this palace is a passage, and the game will not pretend otherwise.

nodes.title: Muqarnas eaves
nodes.card: Muqarnas is a vault built from subdivided niches — literally a geometry for filling the transition between shapes that do not meet. The picture uses it where two impossible planes need reconciling.
nodes.label: Muqarnas eaves over the balcony

nodes.title: The brackets over nothing
nodes.card: Struts carrying the balcony's weight down to a point where the wall below has already ended. The most explicit structural impossibility in the folio.
nodes.label: Cantilever brackets carrying the balcony over nothing

nodes.title: Roundel panel
nodes.card: Blue-and-gold roundels set into the balcony wall — a self-contained pattern field, complete at any scale.
nodes.label: Blue-and-gold tile roundel panel

nodes.title: The lapis court
nodes.card: The upper-left court: a lapis ground scattered with flowering sprays. It reads as a wall, a garden and a page of illumination at once, and commits to none of them.
nodes.label: Upper-left blue tile court with lapis floral ground

nodes.title: The blue niche
nodes.card: A pointed arch of turquoise and lapis framing the green door — the most architecturally correct passage in the picture, and it opens onto nothing the picture states.
nodes.label: Blue arched niche framing the green door

nodes.title: The green door
nodes.card: Green double leaves in a blue niche. Green is Yūsuf's colour in this folio, which makes this the door that matches the man.
nodes.label: The green double door

lock.prompt: Show me what is carried on nothing.
lock.gloss: The brackets descend to a point where the wall has already ended. The balcony is held up by the picture, not the building.

nodes.title: The upper orange door
nodes.card: A tall door on the top storey, its threshold level with no floor drawn anywhere near it.
nodes.label: Tall orange door, upper storey

lock.prompt: Show me the only light in a picture with no light.
lock.gloss: There is no modelled light anywhere in the folio. The flame-halo is illumination as rank, not as optics.

nodes.title: The small tablet
nodes.card: A little epigraphic tablet beside the upper door. Recent work on this folio reads its inscriptions as praise of the painter rather than of the patron — unusual, and part of why the Cairo Būstān matters to the history of artistic signature.
nodes.label: Small epigraphic tablet beside the orange door

nodes.title: The black panel
nodes.card: Gold nastaʿlīq on a black ground, set into the wall like a plaque. Here verse is a building material.
nodes.label: Black-ground gold nastaliq panel

nodes.title: The upper flight
nodes.card: The stair is the barzakh made carpentry: it belongs to neither the storey it leaves nor the one it reaches.
nodes.label: Upper flight of the orange staircase

nodes.title: The landing
nodes.card: A turn in the stair. Read the treads above and below it and they imply two incompatible directions of gravity.
nodes.label: Stair landing

nodes.title: The lower flight
nodes.card: It descends toward the street and arrives beside a door rather than at it.
nodes.label: Lower flight, turning at an angle no stair turns at

nodes.title: The stairhead door
nodes.card: An orange door at the head of the stair, opening across the line of travel rather than along it.
nodes.label: Orange door at the stairhead

lock.prompt: Show me an image held as an image — a surface that is a wall, a garden and a page at once.
lock.gloss: ʿĀlam al-khayāl is the realm where forms subsist as images. The lapis court refuses to settle into any one reading.

nodes.title: The mid cartouche
nodes.card: A gold verse panel laid diagonally on a green ground, following the wall's plane. The text tilts because the building does.
nodes.label: Gold nastaliq verse cartouche on green ground

nodes.title: The muqarnas door
nodes.card: A small door crowned with muqarnas, beneath the stair. The most heavily ornamented opening in the picture, and the least reachable.
nodes.label: Muqarnas-crowned ornate door beneath the stair

lock.prompt: Show me the geometry for filling a transition between shapes that do not meet.
lock.gloss: Muqarnas subdivides a corner into niches until the mismatch disappears. It is a technology of transition.

nodes.title: The door under the stair
nodes.card: Orange double leaves tucked under the lower flight, at the point where the stair's own structure would block them.
nodes.label: Orange double door under the stair

lock.prompt: Show me the isthmus — what belongs to neither of the two things it joins.
lock.gloss: Melvin-Koushki renders barzakh as a joining isthmus between the spiritual realm and the body. A stair is that, in wood.

nodes.title: The iwan
nodes.card: A vaulted recess open on one side — the standard unit of Persianate monumental architecture, here made the picture's structural hinge.
nodes.label: The central iwan — lower arched portal with lapis spandrels

nodes.title: The iwan door
nodes.card: The door inside the vault, drawn in a projection that puts its floor above the vault's own springing.
nodes.label: Orange door inside the iwan

lock.prompt: Show me a pattern with no edge of its own — one the picture had to cut arbitrarily.
lock.gloss: Star-and-cross tiling continues by rule, not by boundary. The frame decides where it stops; the pattern does not.

nodes.title: Spandrel band
nodes.card: An inscribed lapis band across the iwan's head, with tiled spandrels either side.
nodes.label: Inscribed lapis band and spandrels over the iwan

nodes.title: Star tile, left
nodes.card: Green-and-gold star-and-cross tiling: a pattern that continues by rule, not by edge. It could be any size, and the picture cuts it arbitrarily.
nodes.label: Green-and-gold star tile field, left

nodes.title: Star tile, right
nodes.card: The same system on the opposite side, at a different scale, on a plane that cannot be parallel to its twin.
nodes.label: Green-and-gold star tile field, right

nodes.title: The street wall
nodes.card: Plain grey brick — the only ordinary material in the folio, and the only surface not treated as a field of pattern.
nodes.label: The grey brick street wall

nodes.title: The street portal
nodes.card: A pink frame worked with white arabesque, standing proud of the brick. It is the outermost boundary the story has.
nodes.label: Pink street portal — the outermost frame

nodes.title: The street door
nodes.card: Dark leaves with a geometric strapwork panel. In the Qur'anic account the doors are locked from inside; this is the last of them, and the one at which Yūsuf's shirt is torn.
nodes.label: The street door — the outermost of the doors

lock.prompt: Locked from within. Show me plain matter — the one surface here that is not pattern.
lock.gloss: The brick wall is the only ordinary material in the folio. Everything else has been made into a field.

nodes.title: The dado
nodes.card: A deep blue band running the width of the street. It reads as ground, as water and as void, depending on what you take the wall above it to be.
nodes.label: Dark blue dado band at street level

nodes.title: The upper verses
nodes.card: Verse cartouches set into the roofline, following the wall planes rather than the page — while the page's own margin is left blank.
nodes.label: Nastaliq verse cartouches across the top

nodes.title: Upper-left verse
nodes.card: A cartouche wedged into the corner of the court, angled to the wall it sits on.
nodes.label: Nastaliq verse cartouche, upper left

nodes.title: The foot verses
nodes.card: Two blocks of nastaʿlīq at the base — the only text in the folio still behaving like text on a page.
nodes.label: Nastaliq verse cartouches along the foot
